note: NPC lines and the opening chain's script. {rider} is the rider's name, {short} is how much money is missing. Speaker narrator has no name box.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your first bike: a tired 50cc, bought with everything you had. You kick it over. Nothing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Phoenix MX, the garage on the high street, fixes anything with an engine. Go and see the town's mechanic there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Press Tab or tap Bike to check your bike, your bag and your current task.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: So you're the new rider everyone's on about? Paul Phoenix. This is my place. Let's have a listen to that 50.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Paul pulls the plug, squints at it, and shakes his head.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Top end's gone. Zero compression. That bike's going nowhere until it's replaced.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Here, take this used top end. It's off a customer's old bike and it's still got plenty of life in it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I haven't got any tools.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: No, you'd need a proper workshop for that. Use my bench. It's £90 for bench time and the gaskets. Fit it and I'll pay you £120 for helping out after.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You got a used top end. The workbench is in the far corner of the garage.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Bench time is £90. You're {short} short.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You strip off the old cylinder head, clean the gasket faces and fit the new top end, step by step.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One kick. Two. The little 50 coughs, then settles into a crackly idle. It runs!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Hear that? Sounds like a bike again. Nice work. Here's the £120 I promised.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: If you're after more, I've got jobs. First, pop up the road to Moto78, Bill's bike shop, and collect my parts order.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The garage order? It's right here. Mind, it's heavier than it looks.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Once you're racing, come back and see me for parts. I stock Grades 1 to 3 for the 50s and 65s.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Lovely, that's everything. Here's £50 for the legwork.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Now, there are two customer bikes on the stands. Give them both a service: chain, filter and a once-over.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You adjust the chain, wash the air filter and check every bolt. That's one bike done.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Neat work. You've got the hands for this. That's £100.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Next, Lee at the tyres and wheels shop has a pair of tyres for me. Fetch them and fit them on my tyre machine.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: For the garage? Here you go, one pair of hard-pack tyres.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Hard pack round here, so you'll want a hard-pack rear on your own bike too, one day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You break the beads, lever the old tyres off and seat the new ones. It's harder than it looks.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Not a pinch in sight. Here's £70.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: One more errand. This cylinder needs a rebore, and the engine rebuilder in the Industrial Zone does the best work. It's east along the main road.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: From the garage, is it? Give it here.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The lathe whines for a minute. The engine rebuilder hands the cylinder back, bright and true.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: There you go. If you ever want shifts, I've always got engine work. So does the fabrication shop next door.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Finish a whole batch for me and I'll let you keep one of the parts you made, as good as whatever you turned it to. Fair's fair.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Perfect bore. That's £80.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You'll want to get to the tracks next, and for that you need a motor. Go and see Jedrick at Nicholls Used Motors, south of here.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Paul sent you? Then you'll want the old second-hand motor out back.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It's high mileage, but it starts every time. It holds one bike, twenty parts and ten tools. Six hundred quid, no haggling.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll come back when I've got the money.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Six hundred for the motor? Fair price. Here's £40 extra for all your help today.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: If you're still short, the fabrication shop and the engine rebuilder always need shift workers.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Six hundred, and you're {short} short. Shifts in the Industrial Zone pay. Come back when you've got it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Pleasure doing business. Here are the keys. I've parked it outside your room.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Load your bike and your spares before you set off. A rider without spares is a spectator.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You wheel the bike up the ramp, strap it down, then load your spares and tools.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Everything has its place. Ready to go racing.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Got yourself a motor, I see. Then you're a proper racer now.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Try Farmland MX first. It's hard pack, flowing, and good for a first race. Take the west road out of town.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The council's just finished the roadworks on it, so you're in luck.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: There are two more down the same road: Riverside Arena by the river, and Longmoor Enduro out in the woods.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: See you on the gate.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Not now, I'm in the middle of something. Check your task.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: How's the 50 running? Bring it round if you need bench time.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Treat that motor right and it'll get you to every track in the area.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I still race when I can get away from the forecourt. See you on the gate, and don't expect me to move over.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Bill Rothon, Moto78. Parts for 50s and 65s, Grades 1 to 3. Have a look at the counter.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I race too, when the shop lets me. Everything on these shelves I've broken myself at some point, so I know what lasts.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Lee Stocky. Tyres, rims, spokes and brakes. Hard pack round here, so you'll want a hard-pack rear.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I won the Sprocket Cup a few seasons back, before the injury. I'm getting back on the bike this season, so you'll see me at the odd race.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Howzit. Jason Styles, J's Tools. Came over from South Africa chasing the dream, and I'm still chasing it: this is the season, I can feel it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Tool sets, one per part group. Buy a set once and it's yours for good. With the right set you repair and fit those parts yourself, at your tool cabinet at home or out of the back of your motor, and it costs you nothing but the grade.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Looking for shifts? Use the blue bench inside to start a batch of frame brackets. It's £3 a bracket.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Finish the batch and one of them's yours to keep. Stop whenever you like; it'll be waiting for you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Want a shift? Start at the long bench inside. It's £2.50 a piston, and one part from every finished batch is yours to keep.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Do enough work for me and I might let you use the practice yard.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Louis Jonez, Home Town Local Champion. You race? There are three local tracks round here, but you'll need a motor to reach them.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Farmland MX, west road. I'll see you on the gate.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Hello there! I'm Joseph Halden. My family runs every track in the land: Farmland MX, Riverside Arena, Longmoor Enduro, the lot.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It started with Farmland. That track used to be our family's farm, and every bump out there has a story. The rest came along as the sport grew.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You'll find me in the race office at every one of them. First time racing with us, {rider}? Your first race day is free. Sign on when you're ready, and have fun out there.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Good to see you, {rider}. Sign on here for race days and practice, same as at all our tracks.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: New face. Brandon Stocky, Sprocket Cup Champion. My dad runs Lee's T's and Wheels, so I've had good tyres under me since I could walk.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I've beaten everyone round here. I'm looking for my next worthy opponent. Signing on for the 50s? Maybe it's you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Not bad out there. I'm still the Sprocket Cup Champion, mind. Keep that up and you might be the worthy opponent I've been waiting for.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: This old machine? Put a clean part in and see what comes out. Not today, though.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Hi {rider}! I coach the running club. Riders forget it, but a moto is hard work. The fitter you are, the less you fade at the end.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Fancy a session? Keep to the pace I set for each lap. Every session builds your Endurance.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Oh, hello! I'm always on this computer. Pop round any time.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Now you've got the bike running, here's some advice. Racing comes down to two things: you and your bike.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ride, train and race to level up your skills. Every lap teaches you something.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Parts wear out as you ride. Keep an eye on them in your bike panel, and upgrade to better grades when you can afford it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I can repair a worn part here. It comes back one grade lower, but good as new. Grade 1 parts and broken parts can't be repaired, though. Those have to be replaced.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Oh, and there's a cocky lad by the practice track gate, Mickey Alington. He says nobody in town can beat him. Fancy proving him wrong?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Heard you've been helping out round town. Good on you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Keep an eye out for Dan Smyth by the practice yard down the road. He's always causing trouble and telling everyone he's the fastest in the zone.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Look after your bike, and you might just beat him at his own game.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: And if you want shifts, use the blue bench inside to start a batch of frame brackets. It's £3 a bracket.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Hello there! Got a minute? This old part's seen better days, and I'm far too busy to take it in myself.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Could you get it repaired at the garage and bring it back? I'll pay you back what the repair costs, plus £5 for your trouble.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Any luck with my part? The garage on the high street can repair it. Remember, it's mine, so look after it!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Good as new! Thanks a lot. Here's the repair money back, plus a little extra.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Come and see me again. There's always something here that needs fixing.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You? Race me? I might be stuck kicking my bike over now and then, but once she gets going, she's a rocket.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: They're building a brand new track here. Soon as it opens, I'll race you for £50 and show you what she can do.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Back for more? It's £50 to race me. Eight of us, three laps.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Win, and you get your £50 back plus £50 more. Anything but first, and I keep it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You need £50 to race me. Come back when you've got it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: What? You beat me! Lucky day, that's all. Here's your money.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Rematch? Any time you like.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Told you I'm the fastest round here! Come back and try again whenever you like.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Your bike sounded a bit tired out there. Look after it and you'll give me a proper race.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Your bike's quick enough. It's your riding that needs a bit more practice.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Your bike's quick enough, but you looked worn out by the end. Get a bit fitter and you'll be right there.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Your bike's definitely quick enough. You were just unlucky today. Have another go!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Looking for trouble? I'd race you, but they're still building the new track in the yard.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Come back when it's done. Just you and me, £70, winner takes it all.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: So you want to race me? Just you and me, three laps, and it costs £70.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Beat me and you get your £70 back plus £70 more. Lose, and I keep it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: £70 or no race. Go and do some shifts, then come back.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: No way! Nobody beats me in the zone. Fine, here's your money.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I want a rematch. Same time, same place.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ha! Too slow. The zone is mine. Come back when you think you're ready.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Sprocket Cup champion! Well ridden, {rider}. That's one for the board in the office.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Before you head off: Bill at Moto78 in Home Town has your 65cc waiting. Go and sort it out with him.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: And keep an ear out. There's talk of the road to Mountain Town opening up.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: There's the Sprocket Cup champion! Joseph rang ahead. Your 65cc is ready when you are.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take the champion's sponsor's bike, or buy a stock one. Have a look.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Oh, and Manny Festo was in asking after you. He's got news about the road to Mountain Town. You'll find him here in Home Town.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Manny Festo with the news! Sprocket Cup champion, {rider}. Congratulations!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The road to Mountain Town stays shut until you win the Sprocket Cup. Win it and the barrier comes up.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Come back and see me when you've won it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Manny Festo! Told you I'd see you here. Welcome to Mountain Town: clay, rain and more rain.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Taylor Heart is the Chain Cup Champion and Andy McLaren the Local Champion. Andy's the one you want: he opens the tracks round here.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The same faces run the shops: Paul, Bill, Lee and Jedrick all came up the valley with you. Paul's got something new on the racks.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: There you are! Mountain Town. Bigger bikes, wetter tracks and a champion who's worked his whole life for his title.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Go and see Paul at Phoenix MX first. He wants a word about what's new up here.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Good, you made it. Same garage, new town: repairs, the bench, the job board, and now a clothing rack by the door.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The rack's shut till you've got a wardrobe to hang things in. The Starter terrace by the road is for sale: buy it and the rack opens.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: While you're here: take this parts order up to Lee at the tyre shop. He's waiting on it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's my order! Cheers. Paul said you'd be along.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Wheels and tyres, same as ever, Grades 1 to 4 up here. And I'm racing again this season, so I'll see you at the gate.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You'll be the rider Paul mentioned. This is the Wheel works: we lace and true wheels for half the valley.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Work a batch of 50 and you're paid £2 a wheel, Wheels XP every pass, and when the batch is done the best wheel of the lot is yours to keep.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Start at the blue bench when you're ready. Stop whenever you like: the batch waits for you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The gym? Through here. Weights build Strength, and Strength is what keeps a 65 pointed straight through the clay.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A round is forty seconds. Press on the beat, and every round counts whatever you lift. Come back whenever you want.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Andy McLaren. Mountain Town Local Champion. Nobody ever handed me a thing: I worked all my life to win this title, and I ain't giving it up easy.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The tracks are open to you now: Clayhill MX, Valley Arena and Bog End Enduro. Sign on with Joseph at any race office.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Win the Mountain Town Local Champion here and the Mountain Town badge is yours. Then it's Taylor Heart for the Chain Cup, and I'd bring a towel.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Phoenix MX, Mountain Town branch. Repairs, the bench, the job board, and the clothing rack once you've a wardrobe to use.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Jedrick Nicholls, still the man for motors. Up here I've got the Old Rusty Van: twice the room of the truck, with yours in part exchange.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Moto78! Bigger shelves up here: engine, suspension and bodywork to Grade 4, for the 50s, 65s and the 85 small wheels.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Lee's T's & Wheels. Wheels, tyres and brakes to Grade 4. Mud tyres are the ones you want up here.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Wheel works. Fifty wheels a batch, £2 each, Wheels XP every pass, and the best wheel's yours when the batch is done. Blue bench to start.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Andy McLaren, Mountain Town Local Champion. Took me years of graft and no help to get here, so don't expect me to hand it over. Enter the Mountain Town Local Champion at any race office if you fancy trying.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The badge is yours, fair and square. Taylor Heart's next: the Chain Cup, six rounds. Go on then.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Taylor Heart. Chain Cup Champion, three years running. The Chain Cup is six rounds, two at every track, and I win most of them.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You beat me. Properly. The road east is open and Beach Town's waiting. Don't forget where you learned to ride in the wet.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Town gym. Weights for Strength. Forty seconds a round, press on the beat, and every round counts.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The practice yard's yours: body position, cone braking and rut riding. Pick a drill. Every round counts.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Kyle Brooks. I've a race for you, but my forks are shot and I'm skint. Get them repaired for me and I'll race you for £80 on my own track.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Forks sorted? Then let's race. £80 says you can't live with me on the mountain loop.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Come back with £80. I don't race for nothing.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You had me there. Take it: you earned it. Rematch any time.

lines.speaker: npc

lines.text: Freya Collins. Want a race? My brakes are gone and the garage won't look at them till they're paid for. Sort them and I'll race you for £80.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Brakes done? Right. £80, my track, no excuses.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: £80 or no race.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ugh. Fine. Yours. I'll have it back next time.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Thanks for the £80. The rut by the pond gets everyone.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My forks. Dead. Take them down to Phoenix MX, get them repaired and bring them back. I'll pay the repair back plus £10, and then we race.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Forks back yet? Phoenix MX, on the high street.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's them! Here's the repair money and a tenner. Now we race, whenever you're ready.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Brakes. Get them repaired at Phoenix MX and bring them back. Repair money plus £10 for you, then we race.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: No brakes, no race. Phoenix MX will sort them.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Perfect. Repair money and a tenner. Now, about that race.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You're not skilled enough for me to waste my time on. Go and practise, and come back when you're on a 450cc.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Manny Festo, still one town ahead of you. Welcome to Beach Town: dunes, sand and sea wind.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Aidan Borne is the Spark Plug Cup Champion and Justin Smyth the Local Champion. Justin Smyth opens the tracks round here, so find him first.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You made it! Beach Town: dunes, sand and sea wind. The 85cc small wheel class races here, and the shops stock Grades 2 to 5.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Paul, Bill, Lee and Jedrick have all set up shop again. There's a Brake works on the front that's hiring, an agility ladder on the beach, and Big Pete's sand track on the south side.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Big Pete trained half the champions you've ever heard of. If he takes you on, you listen.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Go and see Paul at Phoenix MX first. He's got the lie of the land.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Good to see you. Same garage, new town: repairs, the bench and the job board, Grades 2 to 5 now. Mind the sand: it gets in everything.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The Semi with garage on Shell Lane is for sale, £12,000, with room for the bike. While you're in: take this parts order over to Lee, he's waiting on it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's my order! Cheers. Paul said you'd be along.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You'll want sand tyres here. A normal tyre just digs a hole. Wheels, tyres and brakes to Grade 5, and I've got a brake counter now, with the Brake works along the front.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I'm racing the 85cc small wheels this season, so I'll see you at the gate. Go and say hello at the Brake works, they're always short of hands.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You'll be the rider Paul mentioned. This is the Brake works: brake calipers, 50 a batch at £2 each.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Three jobs to a caliper: turn the disc on the lathe, bore the caliper, then fit the pads and bleed it on the bench. Machining and Wheels XP every pass.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Work a batch and the best brakes of the lot is yours when it's done. Go on, start at the disc lathe and do me one.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Big Pete. I've trained half the champions you're about to race, and I'll train you if you've got the ears for it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My boy's James Nestor. Handlebar Cup Champion, and he learned on this sand. You'll meet him if you're any good.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I'm at the tracks most days too, across the gate from Joseph. Ride your practice with me watching: it costs more, but you'll learn more.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Go and find Justin Smyth first, he's the Local Champion and he opens the tracks round here. Then come back to me. We start with the jumps.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: {rider}. Ride for me today and I'll tell you what you're doing wrong. Costs more than practising on your own, but you'll learn more.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Justin Smyth. Beach Town Local Champion. My dad, Dan Smyth, trained me down in the Industrial Zone.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I moved to Beach Town for a new challenge and took the title.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Did I mention I got the holeshot at Dune Park once? Clean off the gate, first into turn one, the whole field behind me. People still talk about it. Well, I do.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The tracks are open to you now: Dune Park MX, Pier Arena and Shoreline Enduro. Sign on with Joseph at any race office.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Win the Beach Town Local Champion here and the Beach Town badge is yours. Then it's Aidan Borne for the Spark Plug Cup.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Pete's got his eye on you, has he? When I got here he had me on that sand till my arms fell off. Do what he says.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Not bad for a first go. That's a caliper I'd put on my own bike.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Stop whenever you like: the batch waits for you. Now get out on the beach. The agility coach by the hut will have you on the ladder.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Quick feet! Sand makes you work for every step, and that's what you want.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Every round counts towards Agility, whatever the score. Big Pete's track is south of the main road. He'll want a look at you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Again. And again. You're looking at the jump, not the lip. Sand moves under you, so the lip's never where it was last lap.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Feel it through the pegs and go when the front wheel tells you. Now the whoops.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Weight back, front light, throttle on. Shut off in the whoops and the sand swallows you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Better. Come and talk to me when you've got your breath back.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You want to know why they all came to me? Because I tell them the truth.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Aidan Borne rode this sand at twelve. Couldn't jump to save his life. Look at him now, Spark Plug Cup Champion, and he still rings me before a big one.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My James was the same. Fast, and scared of nothing, which is worse than slow.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: So what do I need?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I need to see you on a proper track. Meet me at the Motocross Venue, across the gate from Joseph. No race, just ride, and I'll watch.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I saw. You're floating the jumps now instead of fighting them. Time you learned to use them.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A whip: tip the bike sideways at the top and bring it back before you land. It keeps you low and fast, and the crowd loves it. You'll have it once your Rider Ability's 30.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A scrub is harder: push the bike down over the lip so you skim the jump instead of flying it. That's 60 Rider Ability, and it wins races.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's my lot for now. I'm here whenever you want me watching. Go and win me something.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Justin Smyth, Beach Town Local Champion. Dan Smyth's lad, and the man who got the holeshot at Dune Park, in case you hadn't heard. Enter the Beach Town Local Champion at any race office if you fancy your chances.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The badge is yours, fair and square. I still had the holeshot once, mind, and nobody can take that off me. Aidan Borne's next: the Spark Plug Cup, six rounds. Go on then.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Aidan Borne, Spark Plug Cup Champion. It's six rounds and I win most of them.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You beat me. Properly. The road to Forest Town is open. Go and collect your 85cc big wheel.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Beach agility ladder. Agility ladder for Agility. Forty seconds a round and every round counts.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Big Pete's sand track: jump timing, whoops and sand. Pick a drill. Every round counts, and I'm watching.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You're the one Pete keeps going on about. Ray Crispy. Sidecars. Don't laugh: I've won more sidecar championships than Pete's won arguments.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Sidecars? A bike with a chair on the side?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A bike with a chair on the side and somebody brave in it. The passenger does half the work: hanging out over the chair in the lefts, climbing across the back of the seat in the rights, holding the front down over every jump.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Trouble is, the last few seasons my passengers keep getting hurt. A shoulder, then a wrist, then a knee. Nobody wants the chair now. They say I'm unlucky. I say they weren't fit enough.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You, though. You've got the legs for it. Come and ride in my chair. You'll find me next to Pete at every Motocross and Enduro track.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It's my outfit, so there's no wear on your bike. Entries aren't cheap and we split the winnings down the middle, but you'll come out of it fitter than any gym could make you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Pete's sand's good for the legs. My chair's better. Find me at the Motocross and Enduro tracks, next to Pete.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: {rider}! Ready to hang off the chair? Hold on tight and lean when I tell you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Owen Price. I've a race for you, but my top end is shot and I'm skint. Get it repaired for me and I'll race you for £120 on my own track.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Top end sorted? Then let's race. £120 says you can't live with me round s dune loop.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Come back with £120. I don't race for nothing.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You had me there. Take it: you earned it. Rematch any time.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Told you. Easy money. Come back when you've done some laps.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My top end. Dead. Take it to Phoenix MX, get it repaired and bring it back. I'll pay the repair back plus £10, and then we race.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Top end back yet? Phoenix MX, on the high street.

lines.text: That's it! Here's the repair money and a tenner. Now we race, whenever you're ready.

lines.text: Callum Reid. I've a race for you, but my forks are shot and I'm skint. Get them repaired for me and I'll race you for £120 on my own track.

lines.text: Forks sorted? Then let's race. £120 says you can't live with me round s beach strip.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Come back with £120. I don't race for nothing.

lines.text: Ugh. Fine. Yours. I'll have it back next time.

lines.text: Thanks for the £120. Same again whenever you like.

lines.text: My forks. Dead. Take them to Phoenix MX, get them repaired and bring them back. I'll pay the repair back plus £10, and then we race.

lines.speaker: npc

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Manny Festo, still one town ahead of you. Welcome to Forest Town: roots, loam and wet woods.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Kate Borne is the Clutch Cup Champion and Jeno Rothon the Local Champion. Jeno Rothon opens the tracks round here, so find him first.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Paul, Bill, Lee and Jedrick have all set up again. The Suspension shop is hiring and the woodland yoga retreat is open.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You made it! Forest Town: roots, loam and wet woods. The 85cc big wheel class races here, and the shops stock Grades 2 to 5.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Paul, Bill, Lee and Jedrick have all set up again. There's a Suspension shop on Fern Lane that's hiring, a yoga retreat down by the pond, and Gus Fernley's practice loop in the trees.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Gus rode these woods before most of us were born. Kate Borne learned every line in these woods off him, and look where that got Kate: Clutch Cup Champion.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Go and see Paul at Phoenix MX first. He's got the lie of the land.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Good to see you. Same garage, new town: repairs, the bench and the job board, Grades 2 to 5 now. Mind the roots, they'll have your rims.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The Semi with garage by the road is for sale, £30,000, if you want a bed here. While you're in: take this parts order over to Lee, he's waiting on it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's my order! Cheers. Paul said you'd be along.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You'll want mud tyres for the woods: deep knobs, soft carcass. Wheels, tyres and brakes to Grade 5, the mud tyres are on the rack.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I'm racing the 85cc big wheels this season, so I'll see you at the gate. Pop into the Suspension shop next door but one. Roots are all about suspension.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You'll be the rider Paul mentioned. This is the Suspension shop: forks and shocks, 100 a batch at £3 each.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Three jobs to a unit: strip it on the fork stand, hone and reseal it on the dyno bench, then fill, bleed and set it on the bench by the door. Suspension and Machining XP every pass.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Work a batch and the best forks or shock of the lot is yours when it's done. Go on, start at the fork stand and do me one.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Gus Fernley. I've ridden these woods for forty years and I'm still learning them.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Kate Borne came to me at nine years old and couldn't turn left. Clutch Cup Champion now. Same family as Aidan Borne, who holds Beach Town's title.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Go and find Jeno Rothon first, the Local Champion. Jeno opens the tracks round here. Then come back to me and we'll start on corners.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Jeno Rothon. Forest Town Local Champion. Bill Rothon's my dad, you'll know him from the bike shop.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I've raced my way round the whole land, but I liked these woods, so I stuck around and made the title mine.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The tracks are open to you now: Rootwood MX, Timber Arena and Deep Forest Enduro. Sign on with Joseph at any race office.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Win the Forest Town Local Champion here and the Forest Town badge is yours. Then it's Kate Borne for the Clutch Cup.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Gus has you on his loop, has he? He'll have you riding roots in your sleep.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Smooth. That's a fork that'll soak up a root instead of kicking you off.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Stop whenever you like: the batch waits for you. Now go and see the yoga teacher down by the pond. Every rider round here does it, Kate Borne included.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Breathe out into it. Good. Tight riders crash in the woods, loose ones flow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Every round counts towards Wellbeing, whatever the score. Gus is on the practice loop in the trees. He'll want a look at you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You're braking in the berm. Never brake in the berm. Brake before, then let the wall carry you round.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Flat corners are the other way about: weight on the outside peg, and you make your own grip. Now the roots.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Hit a root square and the front skips over it. Hit it at an angle and it'll have you on the floor.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Better. Your shock's doing the work now, not your arms. Come and talk to me when you've got your breath back.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I raced works enduro for twelve years. Six-day trials, mud to the axles.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: When I stopped, the Borne kids started turning up in these woods: Aidan, then Kate, then young Louie. Louie Borne's the Gearbox Cup Champion in Western Works now, and still rings me when it rains.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: So what's the secret?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: No secret. Set the bike up for the ground you're riding. I've something in the hut for you. Come and see me there.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Here. My old works shock, off the bike I won the Forest Six Days on. Grade 5, and it still works better than most new ones.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It wants a service, mind. Take it to the Suspension shop or fit it at Paul's, your choice.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: And come back any time. The loop's open, and I'll always tell you what you're doing wrong.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Phoenix MX, Forest Town branch. Repairs, the bench and the job board, Grades 2 to 5.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Jedrick Nicholls, still the man for motors. Here I've got the MX Van Medium: more room again, with yours in part exchange.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Moto78! Engine, suspension and bodywork, Grades 2 to 5, up to the 85cc big wheels and beyond.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Lee's T's & Wheels. Wheels, tyres and brakes to Grade 5. The right rubber for roots.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Suspension shop. 100 a batch, £3 a part, XP every pass, and the best forks or shock of the batch is yours when it's done. The fork stand to start.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Jeno Rothon, Forest Town Local Champion. Bill's lad. Enter the Forest Town Local Champion at any race office if you fancy your chances.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The badge is yours, fair and square. Kate Borne's next: the Clutch Cup, six rounds. Go on then.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Kate Borne, Clutch Cup Champion. It's six rounds and I win most of them.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You beat me. Properly. The road to Western Works is open. Go and collect your 125cc Youth.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Woodland yoga retreat, down by the pond. Yoga session for Wellbeing. Forty seconds a round and every round counts.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Gus Fernley, Forest practice loop. Berm and flat corner, ruts over roots. Pick a drill. Every round counts.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Isla Bennett. I've a race for you, but my shock is shot and I'm skint. Get it repaired for me and I'll race you for £160 on my own track.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Shock sorted? Then let's race. £160 says you can't live with me round s woodland loop.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Come back with £160. I don't race for nothing.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You had me there. Take it: you earned it. Rematch any time.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Told you. Easy money. Come back when you've done some laps.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My shock. Dead. Take it to Phoenix MX, get it repaired and bring it back. I'll pay the repair back plus £10, and then we race.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Shock back yet? Phoenix MX, on the high street.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's it! Here's the repair money and a tenner. Now we race, whenever you're ready.

lines.text: Chain and sprockets sorted? Then let's race. £160 says you can't live with me round s logging road.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Come back with £160. I don't race for nothing.

lines.text: Ugh. Fine. Yours. I'll have it back next time.

lines.text: Thanks for the £160. Same again whenever you like.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Louie Borne is the Gearbox Cup Champion and Jordan Styles the Local Champion. Jordan Styles opens the tracks round here, so find him first.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Paul, Bill, Lee and Jedrick have all set up again. The Frame works is hiring and the canal rowing club is open.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You made it! Western Works: quarry rock, old industry and dust. The 125cc Youth class races here, and the shops stock Grades 3 to 6.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Paul, Bill, Lee and Jedrick have all set up again. The Frame works by the canal is hiring, the rowing club's down on the towpath, and Vera Flint runs the quarry practice ground.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Vera was a works rider when works riders were tough. Louie Borne is the Gearbox Cup Champion and Jordan Styles the Local.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Go and see Paul at Phoenix MX first. He's got the lie of the land.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Good to see you. Same garage, new town: repairs, the bench and the job board, Grades 3 to 6 now. Quarry dust gets into every bearing, so keep on top of it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The Detached house by the road is for sale, £80,000, if you want a bed here. While you're in: take this parts order over to Lee, he's waiting on it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's my order! Cheers. Paul said you'd be along.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Rock tyres for the quarry: close-set blocks and a tough carcass, so a sharp edge doesn't slice them. Wheels, tyres and brakes to Grade 6 here.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I'm racing the 125cc Youths this season, so I'll see you at the gate. The Frame works is always short of hands. Go and say hello.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You'll be the rider Paul mentioned. This is the Frame works: frames, 100 a batch at £4 each.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Three jobs to a frame: set the tubes in the jig, weld it up at the TIG bay, then dress the welds and check it at the anvil. Welding and Machining XP every pass.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: It's the only way to a better frame without a sponsor: the best of the batch is yours when it's done. Go on, start at the jig and do me one.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Vera Flint. I rode works bikes when the factories built them by hand, here in Western Works.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The quarry teaches you two things: rock, and patience. We'll do both.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Go and find Jordan Styles first, he's the Local Champion and he opens the tracks round here. Then come back to me.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Jordan Styles. Western Works Local Champion. When I'm not racing I work with my dad, Jason, at J's Tools.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Moving tools round the yard all day keeps me fit. It's how I won the title.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The tracks are open to you now: Quarry MX, Foundry Arena and Slag Heap Enduro. Sign on with Joseph at any race office.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Win the Western Works Local Champion here and the Western Works badge is yours. Then it's Louie Borne for the Gearbox Cup. And win the badge, and the sponsors start ringing.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Vera's got her eye on you? She passed me in the quarry once without me even hearing her coming.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Tidy welds. I'd ride that frame down the quarry face.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Stop whenever you like: the batch waits for you. Now get down to the canal. The rowing coach will have you on the water.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Long strokes, push with the legs. You'll want that engine in the third moto.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Every round counts towards Endurance, whatever the score. Vera Flint's at the quarry practice ground. She'll want a look at you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Stop fighting the rocks. Light on the bars, eyes up, let the front find its own way.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Lift it over the big ones, roll the small ones. Now let's see you pass someone.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You sat on my back wheel for two laps. Good. Most riders charge and bin it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Watch where the rider ahead is weak, then be there before they know it. Come and talk to me when you're ready.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: I worked here before I raced. Welded frames by day, rode the quarry at night.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The works team picked me up off that face, and I raced for them for nine years. Louie Borne came through here too: Gus Fernley sent Louie to me when the woods got too easy.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Do you still ride?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Every morning. Come to the hut, I've kept something back for you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My last works wheels. Grade 6, laced by hand, never let me down on the rock.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: They're yours. Don't hang them on a wall, ride them.

lines.speaker: npc

lines.text: Race department. 100 a batch, £5 a part, XP every pass, and the best of the batch is yours when it's done. The CNC mill to start.

lines.text: Sean Youngy, Capital Local Champion. Never lost a championship, and Neal Borne's next on my list. Enter the Capital Local Champion at any race office if you fancy your chances.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The badge is yours, fair and square. The first championship I've ever lost. Neal Borne's next: the Crankshaft Cup, twelve rounds. Go on then.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Neal Borne, Crankshaft Cup Champion. It's twelve rounds and I win most of them. I'll give you this: you've come a long way from the backyard.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You beat me. Properly. Nobody in the Capital is left to beat. The Legends Championship is next: every MX and SX track in the land. Go and collect your new 450cc F from Bill first.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Recovery centre. Ice bath recovery for Wellbeing. Forty seconds a round and every round counts.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Morgan Hale, National training ground. Pro jump timing, pro gate drop. Pick a drill. Every round counts.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Lola Grant. I've a race for you, but my shock is shot and I'm skint. Get it repaired for me and I'll race you for £400 on my own track.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Shock sorted? Then let's race. £400 says you can't live with me round s national paddock.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Come back with £400. I don't race for nothing.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You had me there. Take it: you earned it. Rematch any time.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Told you. Easy money. Come back when you've done some laps.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My shock. Dead. Take it to Phoenix MX, get it repaired and bring it back. I'll pay the repair back plus £10, and then we race.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Shock back yet? Phoenix MX, on the high street.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's it! Here's the repair money and a tenner. Now we race, whenever you're ready.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Archie Holt. I've a race for you, but my top end is shot and I'm skint. Get it repaired for me and I'll race you for £400 on my own track.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Top end sorted? Then let's race. £400 says you can't live with me round s test track.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Come back with £400. I don't race for nothing.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ugh. Fine. Yours. I'll have it back next time.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Thanks for the £400. Same again whenever you like.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My top end. Dead. Take it to Phoenix MX, get it repaired and bring it back. I'll pay the repair back plus £10, and then we race.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Top end back yet? Phoenix MX, on the high street.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That's it! Here's the repair money and a tenner. Now we race, whenever you're ready.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Maggie. The machine's running, thanks to you. The rules, since you'll forget: a clean part, 80% or better, nothing on it already.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Three modifiers come out, each as likely bad as good, and one part in ten doesn't come out at all. No rerolls. £20 a go at Grade 1 and it doubles every grade.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Here's one for you. Mad Maggie, the scientist with the machine in the Industrial Zone back home? Brilliant woman, bit eccentric, if you know what I mean. That machine's been dead for years.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The Frame works boss here used to work with her. Go and ask. I reckon she'd have it running again with the right hands.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Maggie the scientist? I welded half that machine. It needs two things she could never get: a wound coil, and the Suspension shop in Forest Town makes them now, and a precision valve from the Brake works in Beach Town.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Fetch those and she'll talk you through the fix. Mind, it's a Mechanical Engineer 30 job. Below that you'll make it worse.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A coil for Maggie's machine? I wondered when someone would come for one. Here, wound this morning. Tell her the Suspension shop says hello.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A valve for Maggie? Ha. She's the reason I'm in brakes: she taught me precision. Take this one, it's the best I've made. And good luck with her: she's a one-off.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Going to see Maggie the scientist, are you? Take these two old parts for her first test. She'll want something to put through it before she trusts it, and I'd not risk your own.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mad Maggie, and yes, that's what they call me. You've brought the coil and the valve? And you know what you're doing? Then in you go: the coil behind the dial, the valve under the hopper.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: There. Hear that hum? Years, I've waited for that. Now, the test. Two old parts in, two out, if it works.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Part one in... and, whoops. Gone. Forgot to tell you about that: one go in ten, it eats the part. No rerolls, no refunds, and parts must be clean, 80% or better, with nothing on them already.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Part two in... and out it comes, with Corners up one, Rough down one, Wet down one. Better luck next time, but at least it didn't disappear. It's yours. The machine's open: £20 a go at Grade 1, doubling every grade.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You've got the bits, but not the hands yet. Mechanical Engineer 30 before you touch my machine. Below that you'll make it worse.
